newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Chirac backs Romania for fast NATO entry.
newsitem.headline: Chirac backs Romania for fast NATO entry.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Friday he would press for Romania to be among the first ex-communist countries to be admitted to an expanded NATO and pledged to defend its interests within the alliance.
"I want Romania to join us within NATO from 1999. I am saying this here in Bucharest as I said it London, Washington and Bonn," Chirac told Romania's parliament at the start of a two-day visit.

He said Romania deserved to be included in NATO's first expansion, to be announced at a July summit, after resolving disputes with Hungary in a treaty last year and bringing ethnic Hungarians into its coalition government.

"France will extend you all its support and champion your interests within the European Union and NATO to help you overcome difficulties," he told parliament's two chambers, dominated by centrists since last November's election.

The United States considers Romania a longshot for early NATO membership behind Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic, although it appeared to improve its prospects after the centrists threw ex-communists out of office.
Chirac said France wanted Romania to join the European Union "as soon as possible".
But he gave no target date, unlike a deadline of the year 2000 which he pledged during recent visits to Warsaw and Budapest, where economic change has been faster.
Chirac said NATO expansion had to take account of the interests of Russian, an allusion to Moscow's opposition to enlargement, and warned against creating a "new divide within Europe".
He also urged Romania and Ukraine to settle differences dating from World War Two and reach a post-communist treaty.
